metadata.title: Test fixture: a group whose winner is replaced after a partner tied with it opened (issue #346)
metadata.note: Real DDInter drugs, real mechanism texts, in an order the shipped knowledge base does not have - and the ARRANGEMENT is the fixture. Dolutegravir x Iron / Iron (bisglycinate) / Phenytoin are the same rows ddi-route-variants.json carries, rearranged so that the Iron group is opened by its route-qualified row FIRST, Phenytoin opens SECOND, and only THEN does the unqualified Iron row take the Iron group. All three rows are Major, so severity cannot separate the two partners and their order is decided by bestRulePerPartner alone: a LinkedHashMap keeps a re-put key in its original position and chips Iron first, while a HashMap or a remove-then-put moves it behind Phenytoin. ddi-route-variants.json cannot express this - every group it replaces is either replaced before the tied partner opens, or is not tied with it - which is why this file exists rather than another case over that one. Iron carries no ATC code and Dolutegravir (J05AJ03) and Phenytoin (N03AB02) share no subgroup, so no class-arm sentence folds into either chip.

7199.text: Coadministration with medications containing polyvalent cations such as aluminum, calcium, iron, or magnesium may decrease the oral bioavailability of dolutegravir.

3062.text: Coadministration with potent inducers of UGT1A1 and CYP450 3A4 isoenzymes may significantly decrease the plasma concentrations of dolutegravir, which is primarily metabolized by UGT1A1 with some contribution from CYP450 3A4. Dolutegravir is also a substrate of UGT1A3, UGT1A9, and P-glycoprotein in vitro.

2248.text: INTERVAL: Coadministration with medications containing polyvalent cations such as aluminum, calcium, iron, or magnesium may decrease the oral bioavailability of dolutegravir. The mechanism of interaction has not been established.
